name: site-architecture
description: Plan a website's information architecture: a page tree where every page has exactly one parent, URL rules, navigation labels and breadcrumbs; a link plan computed from a links export (source and target) that uses only your own URLs and shows click depth before and after; hub page and child page link specs; which filter URLs get indexable pages, with the URL count worked out; and a redirect map checked for chains, loops and homepage targets for URL changes and site moves. Not a search audit and not software architecture.

interface.longDescription: Five skills for planning how a website is organised; each gives the plan first, then the problems its checks found. Site architecture turns a page list, menus or a site description into a tree where every page has one parent, a page table, URL rules, a navigation and breadcrumb spec with label checks, and a list of moved URLs. Link plan reads a links export, computes click depth and inlinks, proposes up to 30 new in-text links that use only URLs found in your data, and recomputes depth with the plan applied. Hub design wires one topic's pages into a hub with child pages and a link matrix. Facet policy counts the URLs your filters can create and decides which may be crawled and indexed, with a robots.txt and noindex conflict check. Redirect map builds or checks a map for chains, loops, homepage targets and temporary codes, and gives a launch checklist. Each rule cites a Google Search Central or Nielsen Norman Group page with the date read, or is labelled as this plugin's own default you can change; the plugin gives no traffic forecasts. It reads what you paste and, only if you name your own site and your assistant has a web tool, its robots.txt, up to three sitemaps and up to five public pages. It changes nothing on your site.
defaultPrompt: Laptop filters, single-select: brand 8, RAM 4, GPU 6, screen 5, price 6. How many filter URLs, and which to index?
Plan the URL tree for a B2B SaaS site: 6 features, 40 integrations, blog, docs, pricing. One parent per page; nav spec.
